newsitem.title: UK: Securitisation could cure French property mkt -S&P.
newsitem.headline: Securitisation could cure French property mkt -S&P.

text.p: France's debt-ridden property market could securitize its way out of trouble, Standard & Poor's said in CreditWeek, its weekly publication.
S&P said the French property market has been in crisis since 1991, with estimates showing up to $60 billion of non-performing and sub-performing commercial real estate debt.
S&P said securitization was a potentially cheaper option than selling the debt portfolio as the originator retained the upside potential of the portfolio as the market recovers.

"It's crucial a couple of deals get done to demonstrate to the French market the potential for European commercial mortgage-backed securitization and the liquidity it can bring to the commercial real estate sector," S&P said.
Last week Union Industrielle de Credit (UIC) securitised 1.6 billion French francs in commercial real estate loans.
The commercial mortgage-backed floating rate notes issued by Belenus Securities Plc were secured by mortgages on commercial properties throughout France.
